$comment: Input to `pnpm exec tsx scripts/sanitize-fixtures.ts`: each committed fixture and the raw capture (git-ignored test/fixtures/sgw/raw/) it is built from. Raw files are referenced by capture step, never by a real item id. For USER STEP sources (type user), write ids in urlPattern as {itemId}: the build leak-checks this file and refuses a real id, name or address.
observedSearchUrlNote: The search URL the user's own browser showed in USER STEP S-1 (docs/USER-STEPS/S-1.md step 1); test/unit/adapters/sgw/query-url.test.ts round-trips it.

fixtures.notes: Keyword search, sortColumn 1 (ending soonest), page 1, layout grid.
Second keyword search, layout list. The reply has the same shape as grid: layout only affects the page.
No matches: items [], itemCount 0, categoryListModel present.

Type-valid but meaningless selectedCategoryIds ("abc"): HTTP 200 with ordinary rows, the filter silently ignored. Not the community's 200-with-null-categoryListModel error reply, which anonymous reads did not reproduce.
Non-numeric lowPrice/highPrice: HTTP 400 application/problem+json (ASP.NET Core model validation).
The item page's own call (POST, null body). data is MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss Pacific wall time.
The item page's own call for an open auction with 22 bids, about 30 min before its end.

Same auction as item-detail-open, read about 3.5 h after its endTime: remainingTime "Auction Ended", bidHistory.auctionClosed and isItemEndTimeExpire true, endTime unchanged although the last bid came 5.8 s before it.
Open pickup-only auction (pickupOnly true) with 6 bids, about 10 min before its end; found through a searchPickupOnly ItemListing.
The item page's own Seller/GetSellerInfo/{sellerId} call: the seller's state (Listing.sellerState source for search rows, which carry only sellerId).
The /help page's own HelpCenter/GetList call: every FAQ question and its slug.
SGW's own answer to 'Why was my bid in the last seconds of an auction not accepted?' (S-1 verdict).
SGW's own answer to 'Why can't I bid on more than 15 Items?' (new-account cap).
SGW's own answer to 'Why did the auction I was bidding on end early?' (early end retracts bids).
Rendered (hydrated) item page, logged out, same item as item-detail-open. Contains 5 app-home-product-items cards (seller's other items).

USER STEP S-1 step 6: the logged-in item page's own ItemDetail (same item as item-page-logged-in, show-bid-modal and calculate-shipping). bidHistory.authenticatedBuyerLogin is set (an authenticated read); isHighBidderLogIn false (the user had not bid); buyerShippingAddresses holds the saved address (redacted).
USER STEP S-1 step 7: opened from Quick Bid and closed, no bid. A bare object (no envelope), 23 keys; minimumBid equals the ItemDetail next acceptable bid.

USER STEP S-1 step 8: the reply is a JSON STRING of HTML (shipped-from, carrier, destination, shipping, handling, total; amounts prefixed with a currency sign). The destination address line is redacted. The request payload was not saved (the URL is from the bundle).

USER STEP S-1 step 9: the favorites reply, saved under favorites-page.html (the page DOM itself was not captured). Type=all is inferred from the rows (type Open and Close); the method and query were not recorded. 41 rows, all notes empty. Privacy: startTime/endTime shifted by one salted whole-day constant, catFullName cut to its top level (seller ids are remapped in every fixture).
USER STEP S-1 step 11 (user chose to share): enveloped list; rows carry savedSearchId and the search inputs, no name field.
USER STEP S-1 step 1 (Incognito): rendered search results, grid, 40 cards.
USER STEP S-1 step 2 (Incognito): same search switched to list with the site's layout toggle, 40 cards.
USER STEP S-1 step 4: rendered search results, grid, logged in, 40 cards.
USER STEP S-1 step 5: list via the layout toggle, logged in, 40 cards.
